title: Agent-builder platforms add tenant-scoped flow authorization by Q1 2027
body: Following Sysdig's report of the first in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-55255, a CVSS 9.9 IDOR in Langflow's /api/v1/responses endpoint that lets an authenticated user execute another tenant's flow by supplying its flow ID, the leading agent-builder platforms (Langflow, Flowise, AutoGen Studio and peers) will move per-tenant authorization from an afterthought to a shipped default. Expect object-level access checks that bind every flow, run and artifact to its owning tenant, so a valid session can no longer reach across the shared instance. The forcing pressure is structural: these tools are stood up internally as multi-user 'citizen developer' agent factories where authenticated-only bugs still carry a large cross-tenant blast radius, and Sysdig's own point is that attackers reached for the lower-CVSS IDOR before an older 9.8 RCE. That inverts the usual triage logic and pushes vendors and defenders toward exploitation-prioritized, EPSS-driven patching over raw CVSS ranking. By early 2027 tenant-scoped execution and object-level authorization become a checkbox item in agent-orchestration security reviews rather than a differentiator.

reasoning.because: Sysdig confirmed first in-the-wild exploit of Langflow IDOR CVE-2026-55255 (CVSS 9.9) across tenants
reasoning.given: agent-builders run as shared multi-user internal factories, so authenticated-only bugs cross tenants
reasoning.so_that: vendors ship object-level per-tenant authorization and defenders triage by EPSS/exploitation, not raw CVSS
reasoning.landing: leading agent-builder platforms ship tenant-scoped flow authz by Q1 2027
reasoning.plain_language: AI app-building tools will lock each user to their own flows so people cannot run each other's by ID.

summary: After Sysdig reported the first active exploitation of a CVSS 9.9 IDOR that runs another tenant's Langflow flow by ID, leading agent-builder platforms will make tenant-scoped flow authorization a default by Q1 2027. Attackers hit it before a higher-CVSS RCE, pushing defenders to EPSS triage.
